change: On an MTLPipelineOptionFailOnBinaryArchiveMiss failure the bridge now retries the same render descriptor with the option cleared, compiling the pipeline instead of returning nil, and logs [b4] per compile. Refusal rows also carry the archive seed status.
conclusion: The QuartzCore archive omission no longer costs the render server its pipelines: every creation that used to be refused now compiles, [b3] refusals are gone and CA's failed-to-load message dropped from 45 to 1. Frame pacing stayed inside the unchanged-image spread (25.1 ms interval against 26.5-36.1 ms measured on cadence-b), so the blur/path pipelines were not the frame-time bottleneck. The owner still reports the desktop as very slow.
open: The archive itself is still never seeded from CA: no NativeAdrenoMetal archive row appears, so newBinaryArchiveWithDescriptor: is not on the path CA uses in backboardd; the fallback is what makes the pipelines exist. The wallpaper is a separate PosterBoard crash (configuredPropertiesForPoster: nil assertion), not these pipelines.
